title: Is Your Pet a Genius? The Wall Test Won't Tell You!
summary: You might have seen a funny video online: someone carries their dog or cat toward a wall, and if the pet puts out a paw, people say it's smart. But real animal scientists say this 'wall test' is not a real IQ test at all! Dr. Murat Sırrı Akosman, a vet in Turkey, explains that when your pet reaches out, it's just an automatic reflex—like when a doctor taps your knee and your leg kicks. Vets use it to check if the nervous system is working. It has nothing to do with how clever your pet is. Other experts agree. Dr. Gitanjali Gnanadesikan says most cats and dogs don't even like being held that way. Dr. Juliane Kaminski warns it could be harmful. So, how can you really test your pet's smarts? Scientists say intelligence isn't one thing. Some pets are great at solving puzzles, others have amazing memories, and some are super social. There's no single number for intelligence. A better game is hiding a treat under a cup and seeing if your dog can find it. That's fun for them and actually shows how they think!
why_it_matters: Instead of judging your pet's smarts with a silly trick, you can build a stronger bond by playing clever games that are actually fun for them.

background_read: Reflexes are automatic reactions that help doctors and vets test if the nervous system is working properly.
Animal intelligence includes many skills like problem-solving, memory, and social behaviors, not just one 'IQ' number.

Dr. Murat Sırrı Akosman (a veterinarian from Turkey, a doctor who treats animals), Dr. Gitanjali Gnanadesikan (a scientist who studies animal behavior), and Dr. Juliane Kaminski (an expert in how dogs and humans communicate) all warn against using the wall test as a smartness measure.
Article_Structure: WHO: Dr. Murat Sırrı Akosman, a vet from Turkey, along with other animal experts.
WHAT: The 'wall test' where pets put out a paw when carried towards a wall is just a reflex, not a sign of intelligence.
WHERE: This misleading test became popular worldwide through online videos.
WHY: To show that animal intelligence is varied and to suggest better, safer ways to understand a pet's mind.

perspectives.description: They may be excited to test their pets and see if they are 'smart,' but they could be misled by a simple reflex.
They caution that holding a pet that way can be stressful or even dangerous, and the reflex doesn't measure intelligence.
They emphasize that intelligence has many forms and that problem-solving games like hiding treats reveal more about an animal's thinking.
